key_insight: Human–machine interactions throughout the AI life cycle—not just at deployment—shape the degree of meaningful human control and responsibility in military contexts. Reframing governance to address design, training, testing, and operational interfaces together reduces risks of erosion of human judgment.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap in current policy and practice that treats human control as a single moment (e.g., final switch) rather than a distributed outcome of design, data, testing, interfaces, and organizational processes across the AI life cycle.
method: Conceptual analysis mapping human–machine interaction points across the AI life cycle (design, data, model development, testing, deployment, operation).
Review of governance approaches and case examples to identify where control and decision-making can be undermined or supported.
Proposal of governance priorities and practical levers to preserve meaningful human judgment (e.g., interface design, auditability, testing regimes, accountability mechanisms).
impact: Promotes lifecycle-aware design and governance practices that AI/ML practitioners can apply to ensure systems in military or high-stakes domains preserve human oversight, traceability, and accountability. Encourages embedding socio-technical safeguards early in development rather than relying on end-user decisions alone.
visual_elements: Life‑cycle diagram highlighting human–machine interaction points (design → data → development → testing → deployment → operation) with risk/mitigation callouts.
Control continuum graphic showing gradations from fully human-led to fully autonomous and where governance levers apply.
Checklist or flowchart of governance levers (interface design, audit logs, red-team testing, accountability mapping) tied to life‑cycle stages.
Icon set representing stakeholders (developers, operators, commanders, auditors, policymakers) and their responsibilities.
paper_title: Re-thinking human–machine interaction and the governance of AI in the military domain
